_: A UNIVERSE IS A CARTRIDGE. The engine holds no knowledge of git, of wafers or of grids. It is given a hierarchy that was measured, a placement law for each level, and the totals those levels must sum to. Swap this file and the same engine draws a CPU, a solar farm or a network. Nothing else changes.
name: the estate
subtitle: every line in every file in every commit, copies counted each time
measured_by: tools/clusters.py, walking every path in every commit's tree
cross_checked_by: tools/belt_split.py, an independent walk with identical line and entry totals

also_measured._: an earlier pass the same day, twelve self-hosted runners sharded by content SHA, over 66 repositories rather than 67. Both figures are real; the estate grew overnight by one repository and 132,966,860 lines.

levels.name: repository
levels._: value is entry_lines: every path in every commit of that repository. Additive across repositories with no double counting, because an entry belongs to exactly one commit in exactly one repository.

levels.name: commit
levels._: the leaf level of the measurement. Below a commit the engine draws its lines, one particle each, because the count is known exactly and the positions are computed.

laws._: declared here so a cartridge cannot silently get a law the engine does not have. An unknown law is refused on screen, not quietly replaced.
laws.areal: r = sqrt((i+0.5)/n), theta = i * golden angle. Uniform areal density, so AREA is the share. Correct where there is no preferred axis: gravitational clustering, and a repository's commits.
laws.grid: a stepper grid at fixed pitch, clipped to the circle, with the incomplete steps at the rim marked partial and counted separately. Correct for a wafer, because a scanner steps a rectangular reticle across a round substrate and that collision is the whole geometry.
